title: Review: Proton transfer reactions; Electron transfer reactions

Terms and clues: R3.2#c18 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; R3.2#c24 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; R3.1.4#xt1 term and clue written for the game; R3.1.6#xt2 term and clue written for the game. assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Electrolytic cell
items.clue: A DC power source drives a non-spontaneous redox reaction.

items.label: Hydride ion
items.clue: H⁻, the species that carries out the reduction of carbonyl compounds.

items.label: pH
items.clue: Equal to –log₁₀[H⁺]; a decrease of one unit means a tenfold increase in [H⁺].

items.label: Weak acid
items.clue: A proton donor that is only partially ionized in aqueous solution, such as CH₃COOH.

questions.stem: Aqueous ethanoic acid is added to solid sodium carbonate until the reaction stops. What are the products of the reaction?

options.text: sodium ethanoate and water, with no gas
sodium ethanoate, hydrogen and carbon dioxide
none, as weak acids do not react with carbonates
sodium ethanoate, water and carbon dioxide

questions.explanation: Acid + carbonate → salt + water + carbon dioxide: 2CH₃COOH + Na₂CO₃ → 2CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂. The carbonate ion accepts two protons, forming H₂O and CO₂.

questions.stem: 25.0 cm³ of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ HCl(aq) is placed in a flask and 25.0 cm³ of distilled water is added. The mixture is then titrated with 0.100 mol dm⁻³ NaOH(aq). At what pH does the pH curve intercept the pH axis (0.00 cm³ of NaOH(aq) added)?
Nitrogen has the oxidation state −3 in ammonia, NH₃. What is the oxidation state of nitrogen in the nitrate ion, NO₃⁻?
questions.explanation: O is −2, and the oxidation states must add up to the ion's charge: x + 3(−2) = −1, so x = +5. Like most main-group non-metals, nitrogen has variable oxidation states: −3 in NH₃, 0 in N₂, +4 in NO₂ and +5 in NO₃⁻.

questions.stem: Which half-equation correctly shows the conversion of MnO₄⁻(aq) into Mn²⁺(aq) in acidic solution?

options.text: MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 2e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O
MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O + 5e⁻
MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O + 3e⁻
MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O

questions.explanation: O is balanced with 4H₂O, H with 8H⁺, and charge with electrons: left −1 + 8 − 5 = +2, right +2. Mn goes from +7 to +2, a gain of five electrons (reduction), so electrons are reactants.

questions.stem: Solid sodium hydrogencarbonate, NaHCO₃, is added to dilute hydrochloric acid, HCl(aq). Which statement about the reaction is correct?

options.text: NaHCO₃ and HCl react in a 1 : 1 mole ratio, as HCO₃⁻ accepts one H⁺.
NaHCO₃ and HCl react in a 1 : 2 mole ratio, as carbonates do.
Only NaCl and water form, as neutralization gives salt and water.
Hydrogen gas is released, as acids give H₂ when they react.

questions.explanation: NaHCO₃(s) + HCl(aq) → NaCl(aq) + H₂O(l) + CO₂(g). HCO₃⁻ accepts one H⁺ and the product breaks down to water and carbon dioxide, which is released as a gas: HCO₃⁻ + H⁺ → H₂O + CO₂.

questions.stem: 25.0 cm³ of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ HCl(aq) is titrated with 0.100 mol dm⁻³ NaOH(aq) at 298 K until 50.0 cm³ of NaOH(aq) has been added. Which statement about the pH curve is correct?

options.text: After 25.0 cm³ the pH stays at 7, as all the acid is neutralized.
The pH rises by an equal amount for each 1.00 cm³ of NaOH(aq) added.
The curve starts near pH 13, the pH of the NaOH(aq) added.
At 25.0 cm³ the pH is 7, as only NaCl(aq) and water are present.

questions.explanation: 25.0 cm³ of NaOH(aq) contains the same amount as the HCl, so this is the equivalence point. The solution contains only NaCl and water, and a strong acid–strong base salt gives pH 7 at 298 K.

questions.stem:
Chlorine reacts with aqueous iron(II) ions:
2Fe²⁺(aq) + Cl₂(aq) → 2Fe³⁺(aq) + 2Cl⁻(aq)
Which species is the oxidizing agent in this reaction?

options.text: Fe²⁺, since it loses electrons and so is itself oxidized
Cl₂, since it gains electrons and so is itself reduced
Cl⁻, since it is the species holding the gained electrons
None, since no species here gains or loses any oxygen atoms

questions.explanation: Chlorine's oxidation state falls from 0 to −1: each Cl₂ gains two electrons from Fe²⁺. The species that accepts electrons, and so is reduced, is the oxidizing agent.

questions.stem: In acidic solution, MnO₄⁻(aq) is reduced to Mn²⁺(aq) and Fe²⁺(aq) is oxidized to Fe³⁺(aq). In the balanced overall redox equation, what amount of Fe²⁺ reacts with 1 mol of MnO₄⁻?

options.text: 1 mol
5 mol
2 mol
3 mol

questions.explanation: Manganese goes from +7 to +2, so each MnO₄⁻ gains 5 electrons (MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O); each Fe²⁺ loses 1. The iron half-equation is multiplied by 5: MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5Fe²⁺ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O + 5Fe³⁺.

questions.stem: Methylammonium chloride, CH₃NH₃Cl, is a salt. Which statement about this salt is correct?

options.text: It forms from HCl and CH₃NH₂, with water as a second product.
It forms from HCl and CH₃NH₂, with no water produced.
Its parent base is CH₃NH₃OH, since a base must contain OH.
Its parent base is CH₃NH₃⁺, the cation present in the salt.

questions.explanation: CH₃NH₂ + HCl → CH₃NH₃Cl. The amine accepts a proton on the lone pair of its nitrogen atom, so the only product is the salt. Its parent acid is HCl and its parent base is the amine CH₃NH₂.

options.text: K₂Cr₂O₇, potassium dichromate(VI)
K₂MnO₄, potassium manganate(IV)
Fe₂(SO₄)₃, iron(VI) sulfate
MnCl₂, manganese(VII) chloride

questions.explanation: 2(+1) + 2x + 7(−2) = 0 gives 2x = +12, so each Cr is +6: potassium dichromate(VI). The Roman numeral is the oxidation state of chromium, per atom.

questions.stem: Solid magnesium oxide, MgO, is added to dilute nitric acid, HNO₃(aq). Which statement about what happens is correct?

options.text: MgO and HNO₃ react in a 1 : 1 mole ratio, as NaOH and HCl do too.
No reaction occurs, as MgO is not a base: it has no hydroxide ions.
Hydrogen gas is released, as acids give off H₂ in their reactions.
MgO and HNO₃ react in a 1 : 2 mole ratio, as O²⁻ accepts two H⁺.

questions.explanation: MgO(s) + 2HNO₃(aq) → Mg(NO₃)₂(aq) + H₂O(l). The oxide ion accepts two H⁺ (O²⁻ + 2H⁺ → H₂O), and the salt Mg(NO₃)₂ needs two NO₃⁻ for each Mg²⁺, so 1 mol of MgO reacts with 2 mol of HNO₃.

questions.stem: What is the oxidation state of nitrogen in the ammonium ion, NH₄⁺?
questions.explanation: Each H is +1, contributing +4 in total. The oxidation states must add up to the ion's charge, +1: x + 4 = +1, so x = −3.

questions.stem: Barium hydroxide, Ba(OH)₂, is a strong base that dissociates completely in water. What is the pH of 0.050 mol dm⁻³ Ba(OH)₂(aq) at 298 K?
questions.explanation: Each formula unit gives two OH⁻ ions, so [OH⁻] = 0.10 mol dm⁻³ and pOH = 1.00. pH = 14.00 − 1.00 = 13.00.

questions.stem:
The table shows data at 298 K for four weak bases.
W: Kb = 4.4 × 10⁻⁴
X: pKb = 4.75
Y: Kb = 1.6 × 10⁻⁶
Z: pKb = 9.4
Which statement is correct?

options.text: Z is a stronger base than Y, as pKb(Z) is larger than pKb(Y).
Y is a stronger base than W if Y is the more concentrated.
X and Y are equally strong, as both are weak bases.
W is a stronger base than X, as Kb(W) is larger than Kb(X).

questions.explanation: Kb(X) = 10⁻⁴·⁷⁵ = 1.8 × 10⁻⁵, which is smaller than Kb(W) = 4.4 × 10⁻⁴. A larger Kb (smaller pKb: 3.36 for W against 4.75 for X) means the base ionizes to a greater extent, so W is the stronger base.

questions.stem: What is the pH of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH(aq), at 298 K? Ka = 1.74 × 10⁻⁵. Assume that the equilibrium concentration of CH₃COOH equals its initial concentration.
Which equation represents the hydrolysis reaction that determines the pH of aqueous ammonium chloride, NH₄Cl(aq)?

options.text: Cl⁻(aq) + H₂O(l) ⇌ HCl(aq) + OH⁻(aq)
NH₄Cl(s) + aq → NH₄⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq)
NH₄Cl(aq) + H₂O(l) ⇌ NH₄OH(aq) + HCl(aq)
NH₄⁺(aq) + H₂O(l) ⇌ NH₃(aq) + H₃O⁺(aq)

questions.explanation: NH₄⁺ is the conjugate acid of the weak base NH₃, so it donates H⁺ to water, forming H₃O⁺. This makes NH₄Cl(aq) acidic. Cl⁻, the conjugate base of the strong acid HCl, does not hydrolyse measurably.

questions.stem: 25.0 cm³ of a 0.100 mol dm⁻³ aqueous solution of a base, B, is titrated with 0.100 mol dm⁻³ HCl(aq) at 298 K. The pH curve starts at pH 11.1 and falls gently through a region in which the pH is 9.25 at 12.5 cm³. It then falls steeply near 25.0 cm³, through an equivalence point at pH 5.3, and levels off near pH 1.5 by 50.0 cm³. Which statement about B is correct?

options.text: B is a weak base, and the pKb of B itself is 9.25.
B is a weak base, and the pKa of its conjugate acid is 9.25.
B is a strong base, as the curve has a steep section.
B is a strong base, as the curve starts above pH 11.

questions.stem: Universal indicator shows a different colour at almost every whole-number pH from about 1 to 14. What is the reason for this?

options.text: It is a single weak acid whose one equilibrium shifts gradually across that range.
It reacts with the acid or alkali present, forming a differently coloured salt.
It is a mixture of indicators whose colour changes occur at different pH values.
It changes colour at the pKa of whichever acid is being tested in the sample.

questions.explanation: Each component indicator changes colour over about 2 pH units around its own pKa. Mixing several indicators with different pKa values gives a sequence of colours across the whole range.
